events.summary: Voters in Tennessee's 5th congressional district held a special election on December 2, 2025, to fill the seat vacated by Republican Mark Green in July. Democratic state representative Aftyn Behn challenged Republican nominee Matt Van Epps in a district drawn to favor Republicans and won by Trump and Green by 22-point margins in 2024. An Emerson College poll released before the election showed Van Epps leading by just 2 percentage points (48% to 46%), suggesting a competitive race in what was expected to be a safe Republican seat.
events.why_relevant: The outcome of this special election could materially affect the House Republican majority and signal whether Trump's legislative agenda faces erosion even in traditionally Republican districts.
events.federal_nexus: The election determines representation in the U.S. House of Representatives, a federal body.
events.basis: Voters on Tuesday will cast ballots in a special election to replace Mark Green, a Republican representing a middle Tennessee district who resigned from Congress in July.

events.title: Matt Van Epps won special election in Tennessee's seventh congressional district
events.summary: Republican Matt Van Epps defeated Democrat Aftyn Behn by approximately 9 points in a special election to fill the seat vacated by Republican Mark Green. The district had voted for Trump and Senator Marsha Blackburn by 22 points in 2024, representing a 13-point swing toward Democrats in one year. Election analysts noted the result signals potential Republican vulnerability in the 2026 midterm elections, with special election data suggesting a 7–8 point national swing toward Democrats could shift House control.
events.why_relevant: The narrower-than-expected Republican victory in a previously safe district indicates shifting voter sentiment that could determine control of Congress in 2026.
events.federal_nexus: The special election fills a U.S. House seat and signals national electoral trends affecting federal representation.
events.basis: Van Epps beat out Democrat Aftyn Behn by about 9 points in a district Donald Trump and Republican senator Marsha Blackburn each won in 2024 by 22 points.

events.title: EPA announces revised draft formaldehyde risk calculation memorandum with lowered point of departure and uncertainty factors
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency published a notice of availability and request for public comment on an Updated Draft Risk Calculation Memorandum for formaldehyde under the Toxic Substances Control Act. events.summary: The US military, under direction of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, conducted a lethal kinetic strike on a vessel in international waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing four men described as "narco-terrorists." The strike, the 22nd such operation since September, was announced via video posted by US Southern Command. It occurred amid mounting congressional scrutiny over the legal basis for the campaign, which has killed at least 87 people, and follows controversy over an earlier September strike in which two survivors clinging to wreckage were killed.
events.why_relevant: The strike raises fundamental questions about the lawfulness of extrajudicial killings in international waters, the legal authority for military action against suspected drug smugglers, and the treatment of shipwrecked persons under international humanitarian law.
events.basis: Joint Task Force Southern Spear conducted a lethal kinetic strike on a vessel in international waters operated by a Designated Terrorist Organization. Four male narco-terrorists aboard the vessel were killed.

events.title: TPUSA operations head Kolvet called for drug boat destruction; Hegseth confirmed action
events.summary: Andrew Kolvet, now running operations at The America First PAC (TPUSA) after Charlie Kirk's death, posted on social media: "Every new attack aimed at Pete Hegseth makes me want another narco drug boat blown up and sent to the bottom of the ocean." Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth responded: "Your wish is our command, Andrew. Just sunk another narco boat," and posted a video of what he described as a homicide committed by the Department of Defense.
events.why_relevant: A political operative's call for military action was immediately confirmed by the Secretary of Defense, suggesting that military operations may be responsive to partisan political pressure rather than independent military judgment.

events.title: Afghan man shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C.
events.summary: An Afghan national shot and killed two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C., an incident that prompted debate over whether Afghan refugees should be collectively blamed or judged as a group for the act of one individual.
events.why_relevant: A violent attack by an individual of Afghan origin became the factual predicate for political arguments about collective judgment of Afghan refugees and national-origin-based immigration policy, illustrating how individual violence is used to justify group-based restrictions.
events.basis: the Afghan man who shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C. a week ago
